scene: Images of pride's downfall beneath Dante's feet; the angel of humility removes the first P and the ascent grows lighter
story: Dante continues bent toward the ground, looking at the pavement of the terrace. Virgil urges him to notice what is carved beneath their feet.

The stone floor depicts vivid examples of pride brought low: Lucifer fallen from heaven, Briareus struck down, Nimrod, Niobe, Saul, Arachne, Rehoboam, and others; the ruined city of Troy completes the lesson.
The pavement itself becomes a book of consequences. The proud have carried stone on their backs; now Dante reads in stone beneath his feet what pride can destroy.

An angel clothed in white appears near the exit and directs the travelers toward the ascending steps. He touches Dante's forehead with a wing, erasing the first of the seven P marks placed at the gate.
A voice sings the beatitude 'Blessed are the poor in spirit.' As Dante climbs, he is astonished that the ascent feels easier.
Virgil explains that as the marks are removed, climbing will grow lighter. Dante reaches to his brow and confirms one mark has vanished: six remain.

semanticSomatic.semantic: The observer learns from fallen exemplars and recognizes an actual reduction in his carried marks
Pride's consequences are represented as exemplars, not events happening anew on the terrace
The guide directs attention and verifies a transformation that has occurred
An authorized transition erases one mark after the terrace
Burden reduction becomes perceptible as lighter upward movement

alchemicalReading: An example is first seen, then the body is transformed at a witnessed threshold: the first mark is removed rather than merely promised to disappear.
invariant: The mark count changes only at the angel's observed erasure: 7 → 6. Future terraces must preserve exactly six until the next cleansing.
